title: Teach practical AI literacy
description: Explain useful capabilities, limitations, verification, privacy and disclosure.
accomplishes: Explain useful capabilities, limitations, verification, privacy and disclosure. Include a hands-on comparison of a prompt and response using safe examples. Do not anthropomorphise certainty or claim one model is universally best.
prompt:
Act as an instructional designer.

Task: Teach practical AI literacy.

Input context:
- LEARNERS: [LEARNERS]
- LEVEL: [LEVEL]
- CONTEXT: [CONTEXT]
- TIME: [TIME]

Explain useful capabilities, limitations, verification, privacy and disclosure. Include a hands-on comparison of a prompt and response using safe examples. Do not anthropomorphise certainty or claim one model is universally best.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## AI-literacy lesson
Compare a vague request with a bounded task and explicit assumptions. Ask learners to identify an unsupported claim and propose a verification step. Discuss why private information should not be pasted into an unapproved tool. The lesson illustrates critical use; it does not prove that a particular model is accurate or appropriate for every task.
